newsitem.title: CANADA: ALPINE SKIING-RESULTS OF WOMEN'S WORLD CUP DOWNHILL.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-RESULTS OF WOMEN'S WORLD CUP DOWNHILL.

text.p: Defending overall champion and current points leader Katja Seizinger of Germany won the first women's World Cup downhill of the season Saturday by an impressive six-tenths of a second.
Seizinger, picking up speed as she rocketed down the hill, covered the 2.8-kilometre course in 1 minute 41.91 seconds.

Frenchwoman Carole Montillet was second in 1:42.51 and Pernilla Wiberg of Sweden was third in 1:42.64. Defending downhill champion Picabo Street of the United States finished fourth with a time of 1:42.68 and Heidi Zurbriggen of Switzerland was fifth.
Seizinger won the season-opening giant slalom in Soelden, Austria, and has 260 points after four races. Wiberg is second 148 points.
"This is a good start for my season. It gives me confidence for the next downhill," Seizinger said. The second downhill of the season is next week in Vail, Colorado.
